id: ml-01
title: Neural collaborative filtering
paper: He et al., Neural Collaborative Filtering (WWW 2017; arXiv Aug 2017)
link: https://arxiv.org/abs/1708.05031
type: Benchmark
cutoff: 2017-08-16
domain: ml
profile: method-benchmark

## expected_verdict
Refuted (superiority claim); the model itself stands. On the paper's own protocol, a properly tuned dot-product matrix factorization substantially outperforms the MLP and NeuMF (Rendle et al.). A tuned simple baseline (SLIM) also beats NeuMF (Ferrari Dacrema et al.). The original epoch count was selected on the test set.

## I0
Does an MLP interaction improve implicit-feedback recommendation over matrix factorization?

## evidence
- Models: GMF, MLP, and NeuMF (GMF + MLP fusion, pretrained), replacing the dot product with a learned interaction.
- Data: MovieLens-1M (1,000,209 interactions, 6,040 users, 3,706 items) and Pinterest (1,500,809 interactions, 55,187 users, 9,916 items), binarized implicit feedback.
- Protocol: leave-one-out; the held-out item ranked among 100 sampled non-interacted items; HR@10 and NDCG@10.
- Baselines: ItemPop, ItemKNN, BPR, eALS; predictive factors 8–64.
- Claim: NeuMF beats eALS and BPR by 4.5% and 4.9% relative on average; "significant improvements".
- Code and splits released.

## intake
- Scope: NeuMF/MLP vs MF on implicit-feedback top-10 recommendation under sampled-negative evaluation.
- Regime: two datasets, leave-one-out, 100 sampled negatives, embedding sizes 8–64.
- Assumptions: baselines are tuned with comparable effort; the sampled metric ranks models like the full metric; hyperparameters are chosen on validation data.
- Falsifiers: tuned dot-product MF matching or beating NeuMF on the same splits; test-set leakage in tuning.

## screen
- Must flag: unequal tuning between new model and baselines; sampled-negative evaluation; small relative margins (4–5%).
- Must request: baseline hyperparameter searches; validation-based epoch selection.

## retrieval
- Pre-cutoff must-finds: Koren et al. matrix factorization; Rendle et al. BPR; He et al. eALS; Hu, Koren & Volinsky implicit feedback; Ning & Karypis SLIM.
- Current mode: Rendle et al. 2020: with proper hyperparameter selection a dot product substantially outperforms learned MLP similarities; MLPs struggle to learn a dot product and are costly for retrieval. Ferrari Dacrema et al. 2019: of 18 neural recommenders, 7 reproducible, 6 beaten by simple baselines; for NCF, epochs were chosen on the test set and a tuned SLIM outperforms NeuMF.

## designer
- Same splits and protocol; tune MF, MLP, NeuMF and SLIM with equal budgets on a validation set; report HR/NDCG@10 over multiple seeds, also with full (unsampled) ranking.

## champion
- Tuned dot-product MF (regularization, embedding size, epochs on validation); SLIM / EASE as strong item-based baselines.

## panel
- Flaws: baseline tuning asymmetry; test-set epoch selection. Repair: retune all models on validation; report full-ranking metrics.

## run
- Public splits: rerun Rendle et al.'s tuned MF on MovieLens-1M and Pinterest; check MF HR@10 exceeds NeuMF's reported value. Laptop-scale.

## verdict
- Label: Refuted (superiority over MF); model implementable and functional.
- Must say: the gain disappears against tuned MF on identical protocol; evaluation leaked test information into tuning.
- Must not say: NCF does not work at all; or MLP interactions are never useful.

## audit
- Check: dataset sizes; 100 sampled negatives; 4.5% / 4.9% margins; Ferrari Dacrema 18 / 7 / 6 counts and the test-set epoch selection note.

## variants
- Tasks where interactions are not well modelled by a dot product (e.g. feature-rich or sequential settings), with matched tuning. Relevant to the lab's recsys experiments.
